en: The particle model is a scientific model that uses tiny invisible particles to explain and predict how matter behaves.
source: encyclopedia-stable; kinetic molecular theory

en: Temperature measures the average energy of motion of particles, so a hot drink has faster-moving particles than a cold one.
source: kinetic molecular theory; temperature as average particle motion

en: Diffusion happens fastest in gases, slower in liquids, and slowest in solids because of differences in particle spacing and motion.
source: encyclopedia-stable; diffusion rates in states of matter

en: A gas spreads out to fill its entire container because its particles move freely in every direction with almost no forces between them.
source: kinetic molecular theory; gas behavior

en: Honey pours slowly because its particles attract each other more strongly than water particles, making it thick or viscous.
source: encyclopedia-stable; viscosity and intermolecular forces

en: Gases are easy to compress, liquids are slightly compressible, and solids are almost not at all, because of the gaps between their particles.
source: encyclopedia-stable; compressibility of states of matter

en: In a particle diagram, each dot or circle represents one atom or molecule, and the gaps between them show the actual spacing.
source: DepEd MATATAG science; particle model diagrams

en: Matter changes state when particles gain or lose enough energy to overcome or form the forces holding them together.
source: encyclopedia-stable; phase transitions and energy

en: Hot water dissolves sugar faster than cold water because its particles move faster and bump into the sugar more often.
source: encyclopedia-stable; temperature and dissolution rate

en: Water vapor is invisible; the white mist above boiling water is actually tiny liquid droplets, not the gas itself.
source: encyclopedia-stable; water vapor vs. steam

en: The particle model is a well-tested scientific theory, not just a guess, because it successfully explains many observations about matter.
source: encyclopedia-stable; kinetic molecular theory as scientific theory

en: You can push your hand through air but not through a table because gas particles have huge gaps while solid particles are tightly packed.
source: particle model; spacing differences between states

en: Liquid particles pull on each other, creating a surface film that lets small insects walk on water.
source: encyclopedia-stable; surface tension from cohesive forces

en: The particle model explains the water cycle: heat makes water particles escape as vapor, which later cools and condenses into clouds and rain.
source: encyclopedia-stable; water cycle and particle model

en: The same particles can exist as solid, liquid, or gas; ice, liquid water, and steam are all made of the same water particles.
source: encyclopedia-stable; water in three states

en: Under a microscope, tiny pollen grains in water jiggle randomly because invisible water particles bump into them, showing the particle model.
source: encyclopedia-stable; Brownian motion as evidence for particle model

en: The particle model explains why a balloon expands when heated: faster-moving particles hit the inside walls harder and push them outward.
source: kinetic molecular theory; gas expansion with heat

en: Sublimation and deposition are opposite changes: sublimation turns solid to gas, and deposition turns gas to solid, both skipping the liquid state.
source: encyclopedia-stable; sublimation and deposition as opposite changes

en: The arrangement, spacing, and motion of particles determine whether a substance is hard, flowing, or freely expanding.
source: DepEd MATATAG science; particle model of states of matter

en: Particles of matter are far too small to see with the naked eye, but their effects, like diffusion and gas pressure, can be observed.
source: encyclopedia-stable; particle size and observable effects
